findings: Single PR batches all 4 docs edits + 1 baseline-regen. Each failure was a different root-cause shape so they cannot share one fix, but the iterative `fix → re-run → next-failure → fix` loop converges fast when the gate reports `fail-fast`-style first-error. `--write-baseline` is the canonical regen path; manual row-by-row insertion would be 8x the work for the same result.

Kept Bominal-ADR-0106/0107 citations (those byte-match local ADR-0106/0107 which exist) rather than stripping them along with Bominal-ADR-0133 — preserves the Bominal-inheritance trail per [[bominal-inheritance-precedence]].
fixuptasks: F-ADR-CITATION-KERNEL-BOMINAL-PREFIX-AWARE: the adr-citation kernel (crates/oya-check-adr-citation/src/lib.rs:75..93) byte-scans for `ADR-NNNN` without honoring the `Bominal-` namespace prefix. This makes any Bominal-ADR-NNNN citation either silently pass (if NNNN happens to match a local ADR by number) or hard-fail (if it doesn't) — the silent-pass case is the worse bug. Follow-on slice should teach the kernel to recognize `Bominal-ADR-NNNN` as an external-namespace citation and skip / cross-check against a separate allow list.

findings: Net diff: 4 markdown files touched (1 line each except _TEMPLATE.md at 4 lines), plus 8 baseline rows added. `--write-baseline` regen is reproducible: any future agent running the same command on the same dev tip yields the same TSV. `oya verify --include-deferred` aggregator now reports 47/47 lanes (was 44/47 at session start; +3 lanes flipped this session via PRs #53 / #55 / and this one).

No data-class, autonomy-ceiling, or licence surface touched. ADR-0122 still cites Bominal-ADR-0106 / Bominal-ADR-0107 explicitly. architect.rationale: Each edit uses the canonical fix pattern for its lane (backticks for prose-scanned forbidden tokens, --write-baseline for warning-class lanes, removal for unverifiable cross-namespace ADR citation). Files-of-record kept; meaning preserved.

guardrails: Bominal-ADR-NNNN byte-collision with local ADR-NNNN is a kernel bug (see fixuptask F-ADR-CITATION-KERNEL-BOMINAL-PREFIX-AWARE). Until that lands, any future Bominal-ADR-NNNN citation must either match a local ADR by number (silent-pass false-positive) or be removed. This slice removes the unverifiable citation; a follow-on slice should fix the kernel.

`AAA` in WCAG context is a legitimate acronym (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines triple-A conformance), not random noise. The baseline row anchors it; if a glossary entry for `AAA` lands later, the row can be retired.
